setup_shell.hint: Let the character look at and sort files on this computer by command, when you ask.
setup_shell.onTitle: Let it do things on this computer by command
setup_shell.onText: When on, the character may run commands you ask for in the chat: looking at and sorting files in the folders you allow, checking disk space and the like. Every command is read and sorted before it runs; deleting, using the network and installing software ask you every time, changing files and running programs follow the mode below and your choices on the cards, and some things are never done. While off, no command runs.
setup_shell.onAsk: Let it do things on this computer by command?
setup_shell.onAskText: The character runs commands only while you chat with it and only for what you ask, and works only in the folders you allow. Deleting, replacing, moving out of a folder, using the network, installing software and running programs each show what will happen and wait for you to press “Allow once”. Replying “ok” in the chat is not a yes.
setup_shell.elevated: Mibo is running as administrator, so no command runs at all. Open Mibo normally.
setup_shell.foldersText: In these folders the character may look at files and create, copy, rename and move them; deleting still asks you, and changing a file follows the mode. The first time it needs a folder, the chat asks you too.
setup_shell.modeText: Read only: it reads files in the folders you allow and changes or runs nothing. Auto review: changing and creating files in folders you allow it to sort goes ahead, and Undo these changes under the reply puts them back; a program run in a folder you allow is judged by a reviewer first and asks you only when it does not pass; deleting, the network and installing software always ask.
setup_shell.rulesText: These programs run in their folders without asking. Sending over the network and installing software are never on this list; they ask every time.
setup_shell.addPlaceholder: Paste a folder's address, such as D:\Photos
setup_shell.neverText: Whatever you allowed, these are never run:
setup_shell.logClearText: The commands and their results in the record are deleted and cannot be brought back.

openrouter.name: OpenRouter
openrouter.note: openrouter/free picks one of OpenRouter's free models for each request. The key costs nothing and the limit is 50 requests a day. Some free providers keep what they receive.

siliconflow.name: SiliconFlow
siliconflow.note: Outside mainland China use https://api.siliconflow.com/v1 with a key from siliconflow.com.

zhipu.name: Zhipu GLM
zhipu.note: glm-4.7-flash is free to use. Outside mainland China use https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4 with a key from z.ai.

moonshot.name: Moonshot / Kimi
moonshot.note: Kimi K3 always reasons, so replies take longer. Outside mainland China use https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 with a key from platform.kimi.ai; keys of the two sites differ.

ark.name: Volcengine Ark / Doubao
ark.note: Enable the model in the Ark console first. Outside mainland China, BytePlus ModelArk is at https://ark.ap-southeast.bytepluses.com/api/v3.

minimax.name: MiniMax
minimax.note: Outside mainland China use https://api.minimax.io/v1 with a key from minimax.io.

anthropic.name: Anthropic Claude
anthropic.note: Claude's OpenAI-compatible address takes no JSON mode and keeps no prompt cache, so each turn costs more than on Claude's own API; replies still work.

groq.name: Groq (Llama)
groq.note: Groq serves Meta's Llama and other open models. Llama 3.3 takes no pictures.

ollama.name: Ollama (on this computer)
ollama.note: Enter the name of a model already downloaded. Tools and pictures depend on that model: a Qwen3 or Llama 3.1 class model of 8B or more handles tools, a vision model reads pictures. Raise the server's context length to 16k or more; a 4k default cuts the memory short.
